F1: pipeline.signature` is a hash of the view class names, so `state` is the same for every session. That gives no CSRF protection and lets an attacker replay their own `code` against a victim's pipeline. The fix is a per-session `secrets.token_hex()` saved with `bind_state`, the same as in `OAuth2LoginView`.
F2: Moving on when no Integration row exists is the existing fresh-install path, and failing closed there would break real installs whenever the webhook arrives late. This is a design limit, not a defect the change added.
F3: Rows created through the pipeline have no `sender` (it is set only when present, line 376-377). If such a row is ACTIVE and unlinked, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError and returns a 500 on a re-install that used to work.
F4: Both values come from GitHub's API, so case matches. Exploiting a renamed and re-registered login is unlikely, and switching to the ID is optional hardening, not a merge blocker.
F5: A GitHub network or HTTP failure causing a 500, plus an unlogged parse failure that still shows the error page, is a robustness and observability gap, not wrong behavior.
